Every PLC simulator worth the name has an elevator, because an elevator is the smallest machine that has all the hard parts of a big one: requests that arrive while you are busy, a direction to choose and stick to, a door that must never be open while you move, people who stand in it, and a safety chain that has the final say over the program. The classic student exercise for it, the four-floor elevator with a shaft encoder and a main routine that is nothing but an index of subroutine calls, is the shape this chapter follows. Logix Connect has the machine for it, under File → New Project → Classic: elevator: a four-floor panoramic lift with hall calls, cab buttons, a shaft encoder, a door with its end switches and photo eye, and passengers who press the buttons by themselves. The scene comes with its tags made and an empty routine: this is one to write yourself. The program below is the reference (File → Load Reference Solution: Elevator), built in the order the exercise asks for it.

The machine

The Elevator part is under a new palette category, Classic scenes. Its properties are the building: the number of floors (two to six), the travel time floor to floor, the door travel time, whether passengers call by themselves and how often, and whether the safety switches (eye and overload) are wired. Its I/O is what an elevator controller sees:

SignalMeaning
Call_1 inputHall call button on floor 1 (1 while pressed)
Call_2 inputHall call button on floor 2 (1 while pressed)
Call_3 inputHall call button on floor 3 (1 while pressed)
Call_4 inputHall call button on floor 4 (1 while pressed)
Cab_1 inputCab button for floor 1 (1 while pressed)
Cab_2 inputCab button for floor 2 (1 while pressed)
Cab_3 inputCab button for floor 3 (1 while pressed)
Cab_4 inputCab button for floor 4 (1 while pressed)
At_1 inputFloor switch: the cab is level with floor 1
At_2 inputFloor switch: the cab is level with floor 2
At_3 inputFloor switch: the cab is level with floor 3
At_4 inputFloor switch: the cab is level with floor 4
Encoder analog
inShaft encoder on the hoist: the cab position in counts, 1000 per floor (floor 1 = 1000, floor 2 = 2000 …)
Door_Open inputDoor fully open (end switch)
Door_Closed inputDoor fully closed (end switch)
Door_Eye inputDoor photo eye: blocked while someone is in the doorway
Overload inputCab overload switch (too many passengers)
Up outputHoist motor up
Down outputHoist motor down (never with Up: the contactors are interlocked)
Open outputDoor motor: open
Close outputDoor motor: close
Lamp_1 outputBuilt-in lamp of the floor 1 hall switch and cab button: a call is registered
Lamp_2 outputBuilt-in lamp of the floor 2 hall switch and cab button: a call is registered
Lamp_3 outputBuilt-in lamp of the floor 3 hall switch and cab button: a call is registered
Lamp_4 outputBuilt-in lamp of the floor 4 hall switch and cab button: a call is registered
SignalMeaning
Ind_1 outputFloor indicator 1: the lamp above every door and in the cab that says the cab is at floor 1
Ind_2 outputFloor indicator 2: the lamp above every door and in the cab that says the cab is at floor 2
Ind_3 outputFloor indicator 3: the lamp above every door and in the cab that says the cab is at floor 3
Ind_4 outputFloor indicator 4: the lamp above every door and in the cab that says the cab is at floor 4
Buzzer outputAlarm buzzer

Four things about it are physical, not programmable. Up and Down together do nothing: the contactors are mechanically interlocked, and the log says so. Moving with the door open moves, but the log shouts and the part counts it as unsafe: on a real elevator the door contact is in the safety chain and the hoist cannot run; the part leaves that to your program so you can see what it is for. Levelling: when the hoist drops inside the door zone the drive creeps the car level, as a real one does, so a stop a few counts early still lines up with the sill. And the door eye: a passenger boarding or leaving stands in the doorway for a second and a half, and a Close commanded then does not close (the log notes it).

Two ways to know where the car is. At_1 to At_4 are floor switches, made only while the car is level. Encoder is the shaft encoder on the hoist, an analog word that reads 1000 counts a floor: 1000 at floor 1, 4000 at floor 4, 2500 half way between 2 and 3. The classic exercise gives you only the encoder and has you find the floor values by trial; here you have both, and the reference uses each where it is best.

Passengers: on their own every nine seconds or so (Seconds between passengers), or when you click a call plate, somebody appears on a floor and presses the call button once, a 0.3 s press. When the car stands at their floor with the door fully open they board, one at a time through the eye, and press a cab button for where they want to go; at that floor, door open, they leave. A passenger who has waited 45 s takes the stairs and is counted as lost. The cab holds four; a fifth makes Overload. The displays over every door and in the car show whichever Ind_N you turn on; the call plates and cab buttons light with Lamp_N.

The elevator has three views like every scene, and it opens in the side view, the elevation above, because that is where the machine is easiest to read. The top view is a sheet of floor plans, one per floor, the way an architect draws a lift core: the lobby, the hoistway with its glass walls on four steel columns, the guide rails and the counterweight at the back, the landing doors, the floor indicator, the hall call station with its lamp, and the people waiting. The car is drawn on the floor it is at, fading as it leaves, with its doors, the eye across them, the car operating panel and its riders. The hall buttons and the car’s panel work in the plan as they do in the elevation.

The program’s index

The exercise starts with structure, not logic: a main routine that only lists the tasks, each a subroutine with a flag that says when it is scanned. The flags pass control round a loop: DoNext_Or_Wait (at a floor, door open, deciding) → Close_And_Go (a floor chosen) → Car_Moving (the hoist runs) → Stop_And_Open (arrived) → back to DoNext_Or_Wait. Two routines are scanned every time: catching requests, and the safety chain. Read the main routine like a table of contents:

S:FS is the controller’s first-scan bit, 1 for the first scan after a download or Program → Run and 0 after. These are the tags the program adds to the scene’s aliases:

TagTypeDescription
Served_CountDINTShown on the toolbar: door cycles
Trip_CountDINTShown on the toolbar: trips
DoNext_Or_WaitBOOLFlag: at a floor with the door open; Next_Or_Wait is scanned and decides where to go next
Close_And_GoBOOLFlag: a floor was chosen; Close_And_Move closes the door and hands over to Track_Car
Car_MovingBOOLFlag: the hoist runs; Track_Car watches for the floor to stop at
Stop_And_OpenBOOLFlag: at a wanted floor; Stop_And_Open_Door stops the hoist, settles and opens
Going_UpBOOLDirection of travel: up, latched while anything is wanted above
Going_DnBOOLDirection of travel: down
Req_AboveBOOLA lit request lamp above the car
Req_BelowBOOLA lit request lamp below the car
FloorDINTThe floor the car is at or nearest, from the encoder (1000 counts per floor)
SettleTIMERTwo seconds between stopping and opening the door
Min_OpenTIMERThe door stays open at least five seconds before the next request is processed
Trip_ONSBOOLOne-shot storage for the trip counter
FaultBOOLSafety fault: the hoist with the door not closed, or an overload; cleared by Reset

Exercise 1: initialise

Everything latched must start somewhere known. The car begins at floor 1 with its door closed, so the first thing the program does is treat that as an arrival: Stop_And_Open is the one flag set, and the arrival routine settles, opens the door and hands over to the decision routine.

Exercise 2: catch the requests

The exercise’s trick, and the reason it is allowed to use latches: the lamp in the hall switch is the request flag. Press and it latches; the car opens at that floor and it unlatches. One output doubles as the passenger’s confirmation, the program’s memory of the floor, and, read against the car’s position, the direction to go. The routine first turns the encoder into a floor number and lights the indicator, then latches a lamp for any button pressed for a floor the car is not already at, then sums up what is wanted above and below.

Exercise 3: to the top, and back

The exercise first asks only for this: a call from the fourth floor takes the car up and stops it there. That is one pass round the loop, and it needs every routine to exist with just enough in it. Here they are in the order the loop runs them, already complete for all four floors.

Next request, or wait

Scanned while the car stands at a floor with its door open. It holds the door five seconds (the minimum open time the exercise asks for; requests arriving meanwhile wait, latched), picks a direction, and goes.

Close the door and move

Track the car

Scanned while the car moves. The hoist outputs are latched, which is unusual and deliberate: this routine stops being scanned the instant the car arrives, and an OTE in a routine that is not scanned keeps its last state. With latches, the arrival routine unlatches the hoist explicitly, and a fault that unlatches it is re-energised here after Reset.

Stop and open

Exercise 4: the safety chain, the counts, the lamps

Exercise 5: multi-floor

The exercise’s last and hardest part is already in the routines above, and it is worth seeing where. Collective control means: keep going in the direction of travel while anything is wanted that way, stop at every wanted floor on the way, turn round only when nothing is left ahead, and rest when nothing is wanted at all. The direction is the latch pair in Next_Or_Wait; the stop on the way is Track_Car’s third rung, which only looks at lamps in the direction of travel; the turn-round is the unlatch rungs, which release a direction only when nothing is left that way; the rest is both flags off with the door open. Run it, click the call plates in awkward orders, and watch the displays.

Guided: the elevator

the scene opens with its guided track on (File → New Project → Classic: elevator; or Guided → Guide This Scene: the Elevator on a crossing whose guide was closed). Eight lessons, one routine each and in the order above rather than the index’s: Init (the first scan opens the door), Stop_And_Open_Door (the car stops, the door opens, the passenger steps in), Catch_Requests (a hall call lights its plate and makes a request), Next_Or_Wait (a direction is picked and Close_And_Go set), Close_And_Move (the door is proved closed before the hoist), Track_Car (the car travels, arrives and levels), Safety (the service switch trips the fault) and Ready. Each lesson adds its JSR to the index with the condition the reference has, XIC(Car_Moving)JSR(Track_Car), not a bare JSR, because the index’s conditions are the state machine: an Init called every scan would open the door forever. The reference rungs sit under the fold with hints first, so write each from its comment and ask for the shape only when the comment is not enough; the run checks are the ones a commissioning engineer would make with a hand on the call plate.

Watch for: the lesson order is not the scan order

The track writes Stop_And_Open_Door second and Track_Car sixth, because a door that opens is something you can see on the first scan and a car that moves is not worth having until there is somewhere to send it. The index still runs them in the reference’s order. If a lesson’s run check never turns green, open the Simulator Log: the most common cause is the door check, Door_Closed, failing because the previous lesson’s rung was typed while the controller was in Run and is still a pending edit.

Run it

Run mode: the car settles two seconds, opens at floor 1 and waits. Watch the first passenger: the call plate on their floor lights (the lamp latched), the car closes its door after the minimum open time, the hoist lamp over the shaft comes on, the sheave turns and the encoder counts up, the displays follow the floor, the car stops level, settles, opens; the eye flickers as they board and press a cab button; the lamp for that floor lights. Let it run five minutes and look at the count under the shaft: served and, if the car is slow, lost.

Try It

Set Seconds between passengers to 4 and run: the collective control starts losing people, because a passenger on 1 going to 4 waits while the car serves everything between. Then the harder one: give each hall call a direction, two buttons per floor, and stop for a hall call only when the car is going the way that passenger wants. That is a full collective, and it is the program a real elevator runs. And the encoder exercise as set: delete the four floor switches from Track_Car’s stop rung and stop on LIM(1970,Encoder,2030) windows instead, then find the widest window that still stops the car inside the levelling zone.

Machine faults on the elevator

Tools → Inject Machine Fault… lists the faults that belong to the parts on this floor. Each has a fault card: the symptom, what to watch in the I/O to confirm it, the repair, and what a program should do about it. Repair on an active fault removes its cause the way a technician would; whether the machine runs again is up to the program. None of them is caught by the reference program as it stands: the door-close timeout, the no-motion timeout and the encoder cross-check are the exercises.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: THE INDEX. Every task has its own routine and a flag that says when it is scanned; the main routine only lists them. S:FS is the controller's first-scan bit: Init runs once, on the scan after Run
rungs.words: When S:FS is on, the rung runs the routine Init.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(S:FS) Examine If Closed asks: true when S:FS is on.
  2. JSR(Init) Jump to Subroutine does: runs the routine Init. The routine is scanned at this point, then the scan comes back here.

pats.t: Part of the index: one call, one job.
pats.why: The main routine calls each routine in turn. A routine that is not called is not scanned, however correct its rungs are.
pats.think: a running order on a clipboard: the main routine reads it top to bottom, and each line sends you to a page that does one job.
pats.watch: A new routine does nothing until a JSR calls it. If a routine’s rungs never highlight online, look here first.

rungs.head: Init · Rung 0
rungs.comment: FIRST SCAN: one flag set, the rest cleared. The car starts at floor 1 with the door closed, so the first thing it does is the arrival sequence there: Stop_And_Open settles and opens the door, then hands over to Next_Or_Wait

pred.q: S:FS is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: DoNext_Or_Wait is unlatched, Close_And_Go is unlatched, Car_Moving is unlatched, Stop_And_Open latches on, Going_Up is unlatched, Going_Dn is unlatched, Fault is unlatched, Settle is reset and Min_Open is reset.

rungs.words: When S:FS is on, the rung unlatches DoNext_Or_Wait (Flag: at a floor with the door open; Next_Or_Wait is scanned and decides where to go next), unlatches Close_And_Go (Flag: a floor was chosen; Close_And_Move closes the door and hands over to Track_Car), unlatches Car_Moving (Flag: the hoist runs; Track_Car watches for the floor to stop at), latches Stop_And_Open (Flag: at a wanted floor; Stop_And_Open_Door stops the hoist, settles and opens) on, unlatches Going_Up (Direction of travel: up, latched while anything is wanted above), unlatches Going_Dn (Direction of travel: down), unlatches Fault (Safety fault: the hoist with the door not closed, or an overload; cleared by Reset), resets Settle (Two seconds between stopping and opening the door) and resets Min_Open (The door stays open at least five seconds before the next request is processed).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(S:FS) Examine If Closed asks: true when S:FS is on.
  2. A branch of 9 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(DoNext_Or_Wait) Output Unlatch does: unlatches DoNext_Or_Wait. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Close_And_Go) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Close_And_Go. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(Car_Moving) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Car_Moving. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 4
    1. OTL(Stop_And_Open) Output Latch does: latches Stop_And_Open on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 5
    1. OTU(Going_Up) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Going_Up. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 6
    1. OTU(Going_Dn) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Going_Dn. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 7
    1. OTU(Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Fault. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 8
    1. RES(Settle) Reset does: resets Settle. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).
    Path 9
    1. RES(Min_Open) Reset does: resets Min_Open. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).

pats.why: Stop_And_Open stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

rungs.head: Init · Rung 1
rungs.comment: No requests remembered from before, hoist off: the latched outputs are cleared here because nothing else would
rungs.words: When S:FS is on, the rung unlatches Lamp_1 (Elevator Lamp_1: Built-in lamp of the floor 1 hall switch and cab button: a call is registered), unlatches Lamp_2 (Elevator Lamp_2: Built-in lamp of the floor 2 hall switch and cab button: a call is registered), unlatches Lamp_3 (Elevator Lamp_3: Built-in lamp of the floor 3 hall switch and cab button: a call is registered), unlatches Lamp_4 (Elevator Lamp_4: Built-in lamp of the floor 4 hall switch and cab button: a call is registered), unlatches Up (Elevator Up: Hoist motor up) and unlatches Down (Elevator Down: Hoist motor down (never with Up: the contactors are interlocked)).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(S:FS) Examine If Closed asks: true when S:FS is on.
  2. A branch of 6 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Lamp_1) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Lamp_1. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Lamp_2) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Lamp_2. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(Lamp_3) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Lamp_3. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 4
    1. OTU(Lamp_4) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Lamp_4. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 5
    1. OTU(Up) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Up. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 6
    1. OTU(Down) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Down. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Lamp_1 when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Catch_Requests · Rung 0
rungs.comment: WHERE IS THE CAR: the encoder reads 1000 counts a floor (1000 at floor 1, 4000 at floor 4). LIM windows turn it into the floor the car is at or nearest. Compare with At_1..At_4, which are only made while the car is level

pred.q: Encoder is 499. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Floor is not written (it keeps its value), Floor is not written (it keeps its value), Floor is not written (it keeps its value) and Floor is not written (it keeps its value). None of the branch’s paths is true.

rungs.words: Each path is tested on its own: if Encoder (Elevator Encoder: Shaft encoder on the hoist: the cab position in counts, 1000 per floor (floor 1 = 1000, floor 2 = 2000 …)) is between 500 and 1500, it puts 1 into Floor (The floor the car is at or nearest, from the encoder (1000 counts per floor)); if Encoder is between 1501 and 2500, it puts 2 into Floor; if Encoder is between 2501 and 3500, it puts 3 into Floor; if Encoder is greater than 3500, it puts 4 into Floor.
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 4 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. LIM(500,Encoder,1500) Limit Test asks: true when Encoder is between 500 and 1500. The test is inclusive at both ends.
    2. MOV(1,Floor) Move does: puts 1 into Floor. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. LIM(1501,Encoder,2500) Limit Test asks: true when Encoder is between 1501 and 2500. The test is inclusive at both ends.
    2. MOV(2,Floor) Move does: puts 2 into Floor. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. LIM(2501,Encoder,3500) Limit Test asks: true when Encoder is between 2501 and 3500. The test is inclusive at both ends.
    2. MOV(3,Floor) Move does: puts 3 into Floor. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 4
    1. GRT(Encoder,3500) Greater Than asks: true when Encoder is greater than 3500.
    2. MOV(4,Floor) Move does: puts 4 into Floor. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: A moving value can step over any single number between two scans; a window catches it on the way through.
pats.think: meeting a train. You cannot stand at one exact inch of track and wait for it to stop there; you watch the whole platform.
pats.watch: An EQU on a measured value (a position, a level, a weight) may never be true: the value jumps from just under to just over between scans.

rungs.head: Catch_Requests · Rung 1
rungs.comment: The floor indicator over every door and in the car follows Floor
rungs.words: Each path is tested on its own: if Floor (The floor the car is at or nearest, from the encoder (1000 counts per floor)) equals 1, it turns Ind_1 (Elevator Ind_1: Floor indicator 1: the lamp above every door and in the cab that says the cab is at floor 1) on (and off whenever the rung is false); if Floor equals 2, it turns Ind_2 (Elevator Ind_2: Floor indicator 2: the lamp above every door and in the cab that says the cab is at floor 2) on (and off whenever the rung is false); if Floor equals 3, it turns Ind_3 (Elevator Ind_3: Floor indicator 3: the lamp above every door and in the cab that says the cab is at floor 3) on (and off whenever the rung is false); if Floor equals 4, it turns Ind_4 (Elevator Ind_4: Floor indicator 4: the lamp above every door and in the cab that says the cab is at floor 4) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 4 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. EQU(Floor,1) Equal asks: true when Floor equals 1. Both values are compared every scan.
    2. OTE(Ind_1) Output Energize does: turns Ind_1 on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. EQU(Floor,2) Equal asks: true when Floor equals 2. Both values are compared every scan.
    2. OTE(Ind_2) Output Energize does: turns Ind_2 on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 3
    1. EQU(Floor,3) Equal asks: true when Floor equals 3. Both values are compared every scan.
    2. OTE(Ind_3) Output Energize does: turns Ind_3 on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 4
    1. EQU(Floor,4) Equal asks: true when Floor equals 4. Both values are compared every scan.
    2. OTE(Ind_4) Output Energize does: turns Ind_4 on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Catch_Requests · Rung 2
rungs.comment: CATCH A REQUEST: a hall switch or a cab button for a floor latches that floor's lamp, unless the car is already there. The lamp is the request flag: it stays on until the car opens its door at that floor

1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Call_1) Examine If Closed asks: true when Call_1 is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Cab_1) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cab_1 is on.

rungs.head: Next_Or_Wait · Rung 0
rungs.comment: MINIMUM OPEN TIME: five seconds with the door open before a request is acted on. Requests arriving meanwhile are not lost, their lamps are latched; they wait

pred.q: Door_Open is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Min_Open is reset to 0. It stops at XIC(Door_Open).

rungs.words: When Door_Open (Elevator Door_Open: Door fully open (end switch)) is on, the rung runs the timer Min_Open (The door stays open at least five seconds before the next request is processed) toward 5000 ms (5 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Door_Open) Examine If Closed asks: true when Door_Open is on.
  2. TON(Min_Open,5000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Min_Open toward 5000 ms (5 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Min_Open counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

    Path 1

    Path 2

rungs.comment: The request for this floor is served: its lamp goes out (in the hall and in the car)
rungs.words: Each path is tested on its own: if At_1 (Elevator At_1: Floor switch: the cab is level with floor 1) is on, it unlatches Lamp_1 (Elevator Lamp_1: Built-in lamp of the floor 1 hall switch and cab button: a call is registered); if At_2 (Elevator At_2: Floor switch: the cab is level with floor 2) is on, it unlatches Lamp_2 (Elevator Lamp_2: Built-in lamp of the floor 2 hall switch and cab button: a call is registered); if At_3 (Elevator At_3: Floor switch: the cab is level with floor 3) is on, it unlatches Lamp_3 (Elevator Lamp_3: Built-in lamp of the floor 3 hall switch and cab button: a call is registered); if At_4 (Elevator At_4: Floor switch: the cab is level with floor 4) is on, it unlatches Lamp_4 (Elevator Lamp_4: Built-in lamp of the floor 4 hall switch and cab button: a call is registered).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 4 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(At_1) Examine If Closed asks: true when At_1 is on.
    2. OTU(Lamp_1) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Lamp_1. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(At_2) Examine If Closed asks: true when At_2 is on.
    2. OTU(Lamp_2) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Lamp_2. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(At_3) Examine If Closed asks: true when At_3 is on.
    2. OTU(Lamp_3) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Lamp_3. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 4
    1. XIC(At_4) Examine If Closed asks: true when At_4 is on.
    2. OTU(Lamp_4) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Lamp_4. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Lamp_1 when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Stop_And_Open_Door · Rung 2
rungs.comment: SETTLE: two seconds between stopping and opening, as the handout asks. A door reopened for the eye skips this: it is not closed

pred.q: Door_Closed is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Settle times toward its preset.

rungs.words: When Door_Closed (Elevator Door_Closed: Door fully closed (end switch)) is on, the rung runs the timer Settle (Two seconds between stopping and opening the door) toward 2000 ms (2 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Door_Closed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Door_Closed is on.
  2. TON(Settle,2000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Settle toward 2000 ms (2 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Settle counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Stop_And_Open_Door · Rung 3
rungs.comment: OPEN until the end switch makes
rungs.words: When either (Settle.DN (the done bit of Settle: Two seconds between stopping and opening the door) is on) or (Door_Closed (Elevator Door_Closed: Door fully closed (end switch)) is off) and Door_Open (Elevator Door_Open: Door fully open (end switch)) is off, the rung turns Open (Elevator Open: Door motor: open) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Settle.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Settle.DN is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIO(Door_Closed) Examine If Open asks: true when Door_Closed is off.
  2. XIO(Door_Open) Examine If Open asks: true when Door_Open is off.
  3. OTE(Open) Output Energize does: turns Open on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Stop_And_Open_Door · Rung 4
rungs.comment: Open: hand over to Next_Or_Wait, which holds the door open five seconds and then looks for the next request. Count the stop

pred.q: Door_Open is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: DoNext_Or_Wait is left as it was, Stop_And_Open is left as it was, Settle is left alone and Served_Count is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at XIC(Door_Open).

rungs.words: When Door_Open (Elevator Door_Open: Door fully open (end switch)) is on, the rung latches DoNext_Or_Wait (Flag: at a floor with the door open; Next_Or_Wait is scanned and decides where to go next) on, unlatches Stop_And_Open (Flag: at a wanted floor; Stop_And_Open_Door stops the hoist, settles and opens), resets Settle (Two seconds between stopping and opening the door) and makes Served_Count (Shown on the toolbar: door cycles) = Served_Count + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Door_Open) Examine If Closed asks: true when Door_Open is on.
  2. A branch of 4 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTL(DoNext_Or_Wait) Output Latch does: latches DoNext_Or_Wait on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Stop_And_Open) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Stop_And_Open. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. RES(Settle) Reset does: resets Settle. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).
    Path 4
    1. ADD(Served_Count,1,Served_Count) Add does: makes Served_Count = Served_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.why: DoNext_Or_Wait stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Safety · Rung 0
rungs.comment: THE SAFETY CHAIN in logic: an overload, or the hoist running with the door not closed. The rungs above make the second impossible; the check stays, because rungs get edited

pred.q: Overload is on, Up is on, Door_Closed is on and Down is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Fault latches on.

rungs.words: When either (Overload (Elevator Overload: Cab overload switch (too many passengers)) is on), (Up (Elevator Up: Hoist motor up) is on and Door_Closed (Elevator Door_Closed: Door fully closed (end switch)) is off) or (Down (Elevator Down: Hoist motor down (never with Up: the contactors are interlocked)) is on and Door_Closed is off), the rung latches Fault (Safety fault: the hoist with the door not closed, or an overload; cleared by Reset) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Overload) Examine If Closed asks: true when Overload is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Up) Examine If Closed asks: true when Up is on.
    2. XIO(Door_Closed) Examine If Open asks: true when Door_Closed is off.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Down) Examine If Closed asks: true when Down is on.
    2. XIO(Door_Closed) Examine If Open asks: true when Door_Closed is off.
  2. OTL(Fault) Output Latch does: latches Fault on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Fault stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Safety · Rung 1
rungs.comment: A fault stops the hoist at once, wherever it is
rungs.words: When Fault (Safety fault: the hoist with the door not closed, or an overload; cleared by Reset) is on, the rung unlatches Up (Elevator Up: Hoist motor up) and unlatches Down (Elevator Down: Hoist motor down (never with Up: the contactors are interlocked)).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fault is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Up) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Up. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Down) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Down. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Up when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Safety · Rung 2
rungs.comment: Reset clears the fault once the overload is gone; Track_Car then re-energises the hoist if the car was moving

pred.q: Reset_PB_Pressed is on and Overload is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Fault is left as it was. It stops at XIO(Overload).

rungs.words: When Reset_PB_Pressed (Reset_PB Pressed: NO contact: 1 while pressed) is on and Overload (Elevator Overload: Cab overload switch (too many passengers)) is off, the rung unlatches Fault (Safety fault: the hoist with the door not closed, or an overload; cleared by Reset).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Reset_PB_Pressed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reset_PB_Pressed is on.
  2. XIO(Overload) Examine If Open asks: true when Overload is off.
  3. OTU(Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Fault. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Fault when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Safety · Rung 3
rungs.comment: Count trips
rungs.words: When either (Up (Elevator Up: Hoist motor up) is on) or (Down (Elevator Down: Hoist motor down (never with Up: the contactors are interlocked)) is on) and this is the first scan of it, the rung makes Trip_Count (Shown on the toolbar: trips) = Trip_Count + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Up) Examine If Closed asks: true when Up is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Down) Examine If Closed asks: true when Down is on.
  2. ONS(Trip_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Trip_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. ADD(Trip_Count,1,Trip_Count) Add does: makes Trip_Count = Trip_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Safety · Rung 4
rungs.comment: The buzzer sounds on a fault

pred.q: Fault is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Buzzer is on.

rungs.words: When Fault (Safety fault: the hoist with the door not closed, or an overload; cleared by Reset) is on, the rung turns Buzzer (Elevator Buzzer: Alarm buzzer) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fault is on.
  2. OTE(Buzzer) Output Energize does: turns Buzzer on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Safety · Rung 5
rungs.words: When Fault (Safety fault: the hoist with the door not closed, or an overload; cleared by Reset) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Fault_On (Lamp_Fault On: Lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fault is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Fault_On) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Fault_On on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Safety · Rung 6
rungs.comment: In service: no fault, E-stop healthy

pred.q: Fault is off and E_Stop_OK is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Lamp_Service_On is off. It stops at XIC(E_Stop_OK).

rungs.words: When Fault (Safety fault: the hoist with the door not closed, or an overload; cleared by Reset) is off and E_Stop_OK (E_Stop OK: NC contact: 1 while healthy, 0 when pressed) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Service_On (Lamp_Service On: Lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Fault) Examine If Open asks: true when Fault is off.
  2. XIC(E_Stop_OK) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop_OK is on.
  3. OTE(Lamp_Service_On) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Service_On on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
